newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end down, tracking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end down, tracking Wall Street.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed weaker Monday with the market mirroring Wall Street's slide on rising U.S. long term interest rates, said traders.
Chilean stocks, which have also been hurt by high local interest rates, are seen slipping at the opening but the bolsa could soon hit a resistance buffer, they said.
"The bourse is set to open weaker but could find a new resistance level at 96 points," said one dealer.
The selective IPSA index ended down 1.19 percent at 96.48 points. The general IGPA index slid 0.82 percent at 5,321.23 points.
Volume slumped from Friday's higher-than-average 22 billion pesos to its more recent slack level of 9.2 billion pesos.
Investors reacted negatively to comments from acting Central Bank chief Jorge Marshall ruling out an imminent cut in local interest rates, said traders.
Marshall said the bank would only ease its credit-squeeze once all indicators pointed to a reduction in inflation.
"The measures are having the desired effects and naturally we have to wait for all the results the bank had in mind when it raised rates," said Marshall.

Leading decliners included brewery CCU which dropped steeply on fears that its earnings in Argentina will be hurt by the financial problems of joint venture partner Buenos Aires Embotelladora (Baesa), said traders.
Baesa is in charge of distributing CCU's production of Budweiser beer in Argentina.
CCU's American Depositary Receipts fell 5.06 percent to 18-3/4 while its shares shed 3.13 percent to 1,550 pesos.
Other losers included drug-maker LabChile, down 2.82 percent at 310 pesos and banco O'Higgins which slid 1.96 percent to 1,500 pesos.
Winners included supermarket chain Unimarc, up 4.92 percent at 320 pesos and Banco de Chile C shares which closed up 0.35 percent at 71.25 pesos.
